notes: Three Q4_K_M Nano models, reasoning off and on, via real Pylon CLI and relay. Separate synthetic identities, self buyer only, no receipts.
Off runs include nine original diagnostic prompts; on runs include the same five exact-check prompts. Compare modes using median_exact_subset_pylon_wall_ms, not medians across different prompt sets.

Exact checks include formatting. Generated code and prose are reviewed separately. Model-generated code was not executed.

Direct throughput uses 128 generated tokens, including reasoning tokens when enabled. Including-prefill throughput and engine-reported decode speed are both recorded; these are not final-answer token rates.
Normal Gemma/Clef service paused for each timing run and restored on exit. No quiet lease or Rust builds for this task; competing owner builds continued.

Pinned downloads verified by SHA-256 before loading. Weights staged in temporary RAM-backed /dev/shm cache with a 12 GiB reserve because physical disk space is low. Completed 9B weights removed before the 30B download. These are not permanently installed model files.

Nano 9B v2 uses /think and /no_think rather than the common enable_thinking kwarg. The pinned text-only template maps the explicit mode to NVIDIA chat markers; off rendering checked against the upstream template with /no_think for single/multiturn text.
4B off ran before the explicit --top-p argument and result thinking fields were added; server default top_p was 0.95. Its exact server command is retained.

The first attempted 9B reasoning run stopped before model startup because a transient systemd unit disappeared between SIGINT and stop; the runner now accepts that specific already-stopped state and still restores real failures. The completed retry is included here.

After all measurements, the temporary 30B weight was removed to release RAM for owner work. Only the small 4B weight remains in the temporary cache; the 9B and 30B profiles can download their pinned files again.

```python
def normalize_emails(values):
    seen = set()
    result = []
    for v in values:
        processed = v.strip().lower()
        if processed and processed not in seen:
            seen.add(processed)
            result.append(processed)
    return result
```
